events.title: Pilot Killed As Plane From Remembrance Day Ceremony Crashes In Quebec
events.summary: The pilot of a small plane that had taken part in a Remembrance Day ceremony was killed when it crashed near Saint-Georges, in Quebec's Beauce region south of Quebec City, at around 11 a.m. on 11 November, Quebec provincial police said. Police identified the pilot as a man in his 60s who lived in the region; the crash happened as he was approaching the airport to land. The Canadian Armed Forces said Transportation Safety Board investigators had been deployed to the scene.

events.title: Canada Reimposes Sanctions On 11 Iranian Entities
events.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand announced on 10 November that Canada was reimposing sanctions on 11 Iranian entities under the Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations for contributing to Iran's proliferation-sensitive nuclear activities and ballistic missile programme or to the financing of its malign activities. Canada had delisted the entities in 2016 in recognition of Iran's progress under the 2015 nuclear agreement. The announcement coincided with the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris.

events.title: Storms Cut Power To Hundreds Of Thousands Across British Columbia
events.summary: A series of fall storms has battered British Columbia since 6 November, bringing damaging winds, heavy rain, flooding and widespread power cuts. BC Hydro said nearly 415,000 customers had lost power since the first storm and warned that some areas could be without electricity for days. The River Forecast Centre issued flood warnings for parts of the South Coast and the Pemberton Valley, and the village of Zeballos on Vancouver Island was placed under an evacuation order after a landslide.

sources.publisher: CBC News via Yahoo News Canada

events.title: Carney Government Tables Budget With $142 Billion In New Measures
events.summary: Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne tabled the 2026 federal budget on 5 November, with $142.1 billion in new tax incentives, spending and other measures over five years. The government projected a deficit of $62.3 billion for the current fiscal year and deficits above $50 billion in each of the next four years. The government presented it as a plan to boost the economy and affordability.

events.title: Ottawa Takes Stake Of Up To $1.6 Billion In AI Firm Cohere
events.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on 29 October that Ottawa would make an equity investment of up to $1.6 billion in Toronto-based artificial intelligence company Cohere. In return, Cohere committed to keep its headquarters in Canada and invest at least $1.7 billion in Canadian computing infrastructure by 2030. Carney made the announcement in Montreal as he hosted European Union leaders.

events.title: Bank Of Canada Raises Interest Rate To 2.5 Percent
events.summary: The Bank of Canada raised its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5 percent on 28 October. The bank said global economic activity had remained resilient despite higher energy prices. Its next scheduled rate announcement is on 9 December.

events.title: B.C. Conservatives Win Majority, Ending NDP Government
events.summary: The Conservative Party of British Columbia won a majority in the province's snap election on 24 October, ending nine years of New Democratic Party government. Premier David Eby, who called the vote two years early, conceded and resigned as NDP leader. Preliminary results gave the Conservatives 64 of 93 seats.

events.title: Paul St-Pierre Plamondon Sworn In As Quebec Premier
events.summary: Paul St-Pierre Plamondon was sworn in as Quebec's 34th premier on 21 October, returning the sovereigntist Parti Québécois to power after more than a decade. He named a cabinet of 22 ministers, including one responsible for Quebec independence. He has said his priorities are tackling the province's deficit and preparing for a promised referendum on independence.

events.title: Alberta Votes To Remain Part Of Canada In Separation Referendum
events.summary: Official results published by Elections Alberta on 29 October showed that 74.95 percent of voters chose to remain in Canada in the province's non-binding referendum on 19 October, while 25.05 percent backed starting a process toward a binding separation referendum. The result was a decisive defeat for the independence campaign.

events.title: Four Soldiers Killed In Fire During Training At CFB Wainwright
events.summary: A fast-moving grass fire during a live-fire training exercise at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta killed four soldiers on 17 October and injured 39. A military official later said grenades used in the exercise started the fire, which intensified after a shift in the wind.
